history.text:
Subject: Credit for the outage last week?

Hi Acme team,

This is Neha Kale (Plus plan, Pune - Kothrud area). My fibre was down almost all of Tuesday and Wednesday last week. The router light stayed red the whole time and I had to work from a cafe nearby. It came back on its own Thursday morning, so I never got around to raising a ticket - sorry about that.

Since I lost roughly two days of service, would it be possible to apply a small credit to my account for those days? By my rough maths that's around Rs.150-200. Happy to confirm the exact dates if needed.

Thanks so much,
Neha Kale

Hi Neha,

Thank you for writing in, and I'm sorry to hear about the trouble last week — being without internet for two days while working from a cafe is genuinely frustrating.

I have checked your account. Our records show no outage on record in your area (Baner) during those dates. Outage credits work automatically: when an outage on record lasts more than 24 hours, one day's charge for every day without service is added to the next bill, and the customer does not need to ask for it. Because there is no outage on record in your area for last Tuesday and Wednesday, no outage credit applies for those days, even with exact dates confirmed.

For the future, please do contact us as soon as your internet goes down, rather than waiting. Our engineers can log and check the fault, you will receive updates by email and in the Acme app, and mobile data can help you stay connected in the meantime. If a recorded outage does last more than 24 hours, the credit is added to your next bill automatically — you will not need to ask for it.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Warm regards,
Acme Fibre Support

Subject: Re: Credit for the outage last week

Hi,

Thanks for the quick reply, and apologies for the confusion — my building is in Baner, so your area check makes sense. To clarify, I don't believe this was a network-wide outage: the router light stayed solid red, which suggested a fault on my building's line rather than an area problem. I understand that sort of fault wouldn't show up in your area outage records, which explains what you found.

Given that, I know the standard outage credit wouldn't apply. But I did still lose two full workdays through no fault of my own — missed client calls and all. As a Plus customer of three years with no issues on my account, could I please ask you to consider a small one-time goodwill credit of Rs. 200 towards my next bill? Even a partial adjustment would really help.

Thank you for understanding,
Neha Kale

Hi Neha,

Thank you for the clarification, and I'm sorry about those two lost workdays — missed client calls are a real cost, and I completely understand the frustration.

I have rechecked your account. Our records show no outage in your area (Baner) on those dates, and your account is otherwise in good standing, with nothing overdue. One small note for accuracy: our records show this connection has been active for about 20 months.

Service credits are applied automatically only when an outage on our records lasts more than 24 hours — one day's charge for every day without service is then added to the next bill, and you don't need to ask for it. Since the record shows no outage for those days, I'm not able to add anything to your bill for them. A router light staying red with no area outage usually points to a fault on the line to your building, which is a different kind of issue and one worth reporting to us as soon as it happens.

For next time, a few things will help:
- Please report the loss of service right away, even if it comes back on its own. Our engineers can then log and check the fault, and you will receive updates by email and in the Acme app. Mobile data can tide you over in the meantime.
- If the light stays red again, first restart the router (switch it off for 30 seconds) and check that the cables are firmly plugged in.
- If the internet is still down after that, just reply to us and we will arrange a free technician visit. Visits happen within 2 working days.

I'm sorry I couldn't do more for this one. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Warm regards,
Acme Fibre Support

Is there anything else I can help you with today?
